rose.origin: Asia, Europe, North America, Northwestern Africa
rose.watering: Deep watering 2-3 times per week; moist well-draining soil
rose.soil_type: Loamy, rich in organic matter, pH 6.0 - 6.5
rose.petals: Multiple layered whorls, typically 5 to 40+ velvety petals
rose.medicinal_uses: Rosehip extract is packed with Vitamin C; rosewater helps soothe skin inflammation and reduce stress.
rose.care_tips: Prune dead canes in early spring. Mulch base to retain moisture and prevent black spot fungus.
rose.fun_fact: Fossil evidence shows that wild roses existed on Earth over 35 million years ago.

sunflower.watering: Moderate; water deeply when top 2 inches of soil are dry
sunflower.petals: Composite flower head: 30-70 bright ray florets circling hundreds of disk florets
sunflower.medicinal_uses: Seeds provide heart-healthy Vitamin E and magnesium; sunflower oil is rich in essential linoleic acids.
sunflower.toxicity_pets: Completely Non-toxic to cats and dogs
sunflower.care_tips: Stake tall stalks to protect them from high winds. Water near base rather than over the flowers.
sunflower.fun_fact: Young sunflowers exhibit heliotropism: they track the sun from east to west each day, facing east again overnight.

tulip.origin: Central Asia (cultivated heavily in Turkey & Netherlands)
tulip.sunlight: Full to Partial Sun (4-6 hours daily)
tulip.watering: Light watering; bulbs dislike soggy soil which can cause rot
tulip.petals: Cup-shaped with 3 petals and 3 sepals (6 tepals total)
tulip.symbolism: Perfect and Deep Love, Rebirth, and Royalty
tulip.medicinal_uses: Historically used as an astringent and in soothing skin poultices; cosmetic extracts nourish hair.
tulip.toxicity_pets: Toxic to cats and dogs (bulbs contain tulipalin A and B)
tulip.care_tips: Plant bulbs in autumn before the first freeze. Allow foliage to yellow naturally after flowering before cutting.
tulip.fun_fact: During 17th-century 'Tulip Mania' in Holland, single rare tulip bulbs were traded for the cost of luxury canal homes!

daisy.sunlight: Full Sun to Partial Shade (4-6 hours daily)
daisy.watering: Regular watering; keep soil lightly damp but never waterlogged
daisy.soil_type: Moderately fertile, moist well-draining soil, pH 6.0 - 7.5
daisy.petals: Whorl of white ray florets around a compact central golden disk
daisy.symbolism: Innocence, New Beginnings, Hope, and Simplicity
daisy.medicinal_uses: Mild anti-inflammatory; traditional folk remedies used daisy tea for respiratory congestion and wounds.
daisy.toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic to dogs and cats (contains sesquiterpene lactones)
daisy.care_tips: Deadhead spent blossoms promptly to encourage prolonged continuous reblooming throughout the season.
daisy.fun_fact: The name 'Daisy' originated from the Old English 'daeges eage', meaning 'day's eye', because petals open at dawn and close at dusk.

dandelion.origin: Eurasia, now naturalized across all continents
dandelion.watering: Drought tolerant; minimal supplemental water required
dandelion.soil_type: Hardy in virtually all soils; tolerates poor compacted soil
dandelion.petals: Dense composite head composed of numerous strap-shaped yellow ray florets, transforming into spherical seed pappus
dandelion.symbolism: Resilience, Overcoming Hardship, Wishes, and Emotional Healing
dandelion.medicinal_uses: Potent detoxifier; dandelion root and leaves are renowned diuretics, liver cleansers, and rich in prebiotic inulin.
dandelion.toxicity_pets: Non-toxic (leaves and petals are safe and nutrient-dense)
dandelion.care_tips: Thrives with minimal care; harvest fresh tender spring leaves for salads and teas before flower opening.
dandelion.fun_fact: Every single part of the dandelion plant is edible and medicinal—from flower petals and leaves down to the deep taproot.

lotus.sunlight: Full Sun (6+ hours uninterrupted direct light)
lotus.watering: Aquatic plant; requires 2-12 inches of standing fresh water
lotus.soil_type: Heavy clay or aquatic planting loam enriched with pond fertilizer
lotus.petals: Broad, cupped, multi-petaled radiating corolla with central seed pod
lotus.symbolism: Spiritual Enlightenment, Purity, Rebirth, and Transcendence
lotus.medicinal_uses: Lotus plumule tea lowers blood pressure; seeds and roots nourish cardiovascular vitality and digestion.
lotus.care_tips: Ensure water temperature stays above 20°C. Protect tubers from freezing in winter by lowering containers.
lotus.fun_fact: Lotus petals feature microscopic nanostructures that make them superhydrophobic: mud and water roll off leaving petals immaculate (the 'Lotus Effect').

orchid.blooming_season: Winter to Late Spring (blooms last 2-3 months)
orchid.sunlight: Bright indirect light (avoid harsh direct scorching sun)
orchid.watering: Soak and drain weekly; water only when bark/roots look silvery-grey
orchid.soil_type: Coarse pine bark chip medium with sphagnum moss; no regular potting soil
orchid.petals: Symmetrical bilateral bloom: 3 sepals, 2 petals, and 1 specialized lower labellum (lip)
orchid.symbolism: Exotic Beauty, Refinement, Fertility, and Strength
orchid.medicinal_uses: Used in traditional Chinese medicine for immune modulation and tonifying bodily yin.
orchid.care_tips: Never allow roots to sit in stagnant water. Provide moderate ambient humidity (50-70%).
orchid.fun_fact: Orchidaceae is one of the two largest families of flowering plants on Earth, comprising over 28,000 distinct species.

hibiscus.blooming_season: Spring through Autumn in warm climates
hibiscus.sunlight: Full Sun to Light Afternoon Shade (6 hours)
hibiscus.watering: Consistent moisture; daily watering in hot summer heat
hibiscus.soil_type: Rich, acidic to neutral, well-aerated potting mix
hibiscus.petals: Five large flaring petals forming trumpet shape with prominent staminal tube
hibiscus.symbolism: Delicate Beauty, Fame, Glory, and Hospitable Warmth
hibiscus.medicinal_uses: Hibiscus sabdariffa calyces yield tart herbal tea clinically validated to help reduce hypertension and oxidative stress.
hibiscus.toxicity_pets: Hibiscus rosa-sinensis is generally non-toxic; keep away from Rose of Sharon varieties which can upset stomachs.
hibiscus.care_tips: Feed bi-weekly with high-potassium fertilizer to stimulate blooming. Pinch shoots to promote bushier growth.
hibiscus.fun_fact: In Hawaii and the Pacific Islands, wearing a hibiscus behind your left ear signals you are married/taken, while behind the right ear indicates you are single!

jasmine.sunlight: Full Sun to partial morning sun
jasmine.watering: Moderate; water when top inch of soil is dry
jasmine.soil_type: Light, fertile, well-draining loamy soil, pH 6.0 - 7.5
jasmine.petals: Pinwheel or ruffled star clusters of 5-9 intensely fragrant white petals
jasmine.symbolism: Purity, Sensuality, Eternal Love, and Good Fortune
jasmine.medicinal_uses: Essential oil aromatherapeutically eases anxiety; dried buds infuse celebrated antioxidant Jasmine green tea.
jasmine.toxicity_pets: True jasmine (Jasminum) is non-toxic to pets (beware Carolina Jasmine which is a different toxic species).
jasmine.care_tips: Provide a small trellis or support for climbing varieties. Mist foliage occasionally in dry indoor environments.
jasmine.fun_fact: Jasmine flowers emit their most intoxicating fragrance after twilight, as their aromatic compounds are pollinator-adapted for nocturnal moths.

marigold.blooming_season: Early Summer until first autumn frost
marigold.sunlight: Full Sun (requires at least 6 hours direct sunshine)
marigold.watering: Drought-tolerant once established; water moderately at base
marigold.soil_type: Standard well-drained garden soil; tolerates poor sandy soils
marigold.petals: Carnation-like dense pompons or daisy-like ruffled overlapping petals
marigold.symbolism: Creativity, Passion, Warmth, and Sacred Remembrance
marigold.medicinal_uses: Rich source of lutein for macular eye health; used topically in soothing skin salves and insect repellents.
marigold.toxicity_pets: Mildly irritating if ingested in quantity by dogs/cats
marigold.care_tips: Plant as a companion next to tomato crops to naturally repel destructive root-knot nematodes and garden pests.
marigold.fun_fact: In Mexico's Día de los Muertos, marigold petals (Cempasúchil) are laid out in vibrant pathways to guide ancestral spirits with scent and color.

lavender.watering: Low; drought-hardy once established, requires excellent drainage
lavender.soil_type: Lean, sandy or gravelly soil, alkaline pH 6.7 - 7.5
lavender.petals: Slender spikes packed with two-lipped tubular tiny purple blossoms
lavender.symbolism: Serenity, Grace, Calm, Devotion, and Cleanliness
lavender.medicinal_uses: Linalool compounds induce restful sleep, reduce nervous anxiety, and soothe minor burns and insect bites.
lavender.toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats in high quantities (contains linalool and linalyl acetate)
lavender.care_tips: Prune back by one third after flowering to keep shrubs compact and prevent woody center dieback.
lavender.fun_fact: The name Lavender comes from the Latin 'lavare' ('to wash'), referencing ancient Roman baths scented with lavender flowers.

lily.origin: Temperate Northern Hemisphere (Europe, Asia, North America)
lily.sunlight: Full Sun to Light Afternoon Shade (heads in sun, roots cool)
lily.watering: Keep soil evenly moist during active growth period
lily.soil_type: Fertile, loose, well-draining acidic to neutral soil, pH 6.0 - 6.5
lily.petals: Six trumpet- or star-shaped tepals with long pollen-bearing stamens
lily.symbolism: Purity, Rebirth, Maternal Devotion, and Majestic Splendor
lily.medicinal_uses: Bulbs dried in traditional Chinese culinary soups; used as soothing demulcents for coughs.
lily.toxicity_pets: EXTREMELY TOXIC TO CATS (even pollen on fur or vase water can cause fatal acute kidney failure). Safe for dogs.
lily.care_tips: Mulch the root zone to keep bulbs cool. Snip off pollen anthers to prevent staining on clothes and furniture.
lily.fun_fact: True lilies belong strictly to the genus Lilium; many plants called 'lilies' (like Peace Lily or Water Lily) are botanical cousins belonging to different families.
